evidence.text: earth
Origin unclear.
存也。从土才聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *zlɯːʔ, *zlɯːs): phonetic 才 (OC *zlɯː, *zlɯːs) + phonetic 士 (OC *zrɯʔ).
In the oracle bone script and some of the bronze inscriptions, 才 (OC *zlɯː, *zlɯːs) is phonetically borrowed to represent this word; a phonetic 士 (OC *zrɯʔ) was added later. 士 eventually corrupted into 土 (“earth”).
Probably related to 栽 (OC *ʔslɯː, “to plant”) (Schuessler, 2007).

Etymological analysis: 才 (phonetic)

The database proposes that the original sense of 在 was sprouting, that oracle-bone inscriptions often used 才 for 在, and that 土 was later added in bronze and small-seal forms when 才 was used for talent/ability. This is one proposed account, not uncontested paleographic fact.
evidence.title: 漢字「在」：字形演變

evidence.text: The database analyzes early bronze and oracle-bone forms as 才 plus 士, treating both as phonetic indicators and glossing the word’s original sense as existence. It says 才 was borrowed for 在 in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions, and later records bronze uses for existence/location, including 康鼎「王才(在)康宮」 and a date phrase on a bronze vessel. It reports that 士 and 土 became confused after the Spring and Autumn/Warring States period and that the small-seal form consequently has 土. It also reports a separate bronze use of 在借作士 in the Zhongshan king square pot inscription.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：在

evidence.text: The Han dictionary entry says「存也。从土才聲」, analyzing the received form as 土 semantic plus 才 phonetic. Duan Yucai’s Qing commentary discusses older glossing of 在 as 存問/察 and says the current sense is “exist.” This is evidence for the historical dictionary’s analysis, not independent confirmation of the graph’s earliest formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「在」

evidence.text: The entry for 才 reports oracle-bone occurrence 《合集》38223「才三月」 read as 在三月 (“in the third month”), and bronze examples for existence/location and temporal “formerly” use. It separately records other loans, including 災 and 哉, so those uses should not be merged into the history of 在. The database presents competing views on 才’s own graphic origin: Shuowen’s sprout interpretation and a modern proposal that it depicts a wooden stake/pile, related to 弋; the object identification is therefore unsettled.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：甲骨部件分析—才

gaps: The two main analyses conflict: one treats 才+士 as two phonetic elements in early forms, while another describes 才 as the borrowed whole graph and 士 as a later phonetic addition. Available text summaries do not settle the chronology or prove a simple sequence from 才 alone to 才+士.
The early interpretation of 才 itself is disputed between sprout and stake/pile accounts; no claim here treats either depicted object as established.

The database supplies one Shang oracle-bone citation 《合集》38223 and several bronze examples, but this research did not independently inspect the underlying inscription images or establish a complete dated sequence for semantic development.

The connection between an early sprout/stake graphic and the meanings “exist/be present,” locative preposition “at/in,” and later “formerly” is not fully demonstrated by the cited sources; no chronology is inferred from gloss ordering.
No independent etymological evidence was found to establish the proposed relation between 在 and 栽; Wiktionary labels it probable and incomplete.

The requested official Unicode page for 才 (U+624D) was inaccessible in direct attempts. The local Unihan full file and tracked HSK extract searches did not provide kMandarin rows for 在/才/士/土; only the official 在 record was verified. Local table readings are reported with file/row provenance, not as external proof.
No reuse terms were checked for the recurring databases; no local extract is recommended on the basis of this limited review.

The earliest attestation report for 才 used as 在 is 《合集》38223, glossed “in the third month”; the underlying inscription image and its specific archaeological date were not independently inspected here.

The original referent and ancient name/pronunciation of 才 are unsettled between sprout and stake/pile analyses. No independent sound evidence for the pictured object’s name was established; accordingly no etymology based on the object’s name is proposed.

The competing accounts do not establish a complete dated chain from a single 才 graph to 才+士 and then 土. CUHK dates the 士/土 confusion broadly to after Spring and Autumn/Warring States; Sinica describes a 土 addition, while Wiktionary describes a later added 士 that became 土.

Earliest semantics remain incompletely documented: reported oracle-bone 才三月 supports a locative/date use; bronze evidence cited by CUHK includes existence/location, “formerly,” and a locative preposition. Those examples do not establish every semantic transition or exact chronology.

Baxter–Sagart comparisons were checked against the specified local rows; the direct official Unihan records for U+5728, U+624D, and U+58EB could not be verified by the browser. Local kMandarin values are not presented as external Unihan page evidence.

The source’s probable relationship of 在 to 栽 was not independently substantiated. No extract of recurring databases is recommended because reuse terms for their textual data were not checked and a repeatable extract’s editorial value was not demonstrated.

Only the 在 oracle-script and Shuowen seal-script redraws were verified with exact Commons file pages and reuse terms. Exact file URLs were established from those pages; image downloads themselves were inaccessible to the browser, so no pixel inspection is claimed.

CUHK’s account of early 才+士 and the Sinica account in the supplied dossier, which describes 才 used for 在 and 土 added later, remain in conflict; the consulted pages do not establish a complete dated graphic sequence.

The ancient graphic referent and original name/pronunciation of 才 remain unsettled. The reported phonetic-loan use of 才 for 在 is independent of identifying that object, so no object-name etymology is asserted.
The oracle-bone and bronze examples are reported by CUHK, but the underlying inscription images were not independently inspected and their exact archaeological dates were not established here.

The relation between the early reported date/location uses and meanings such as existence, general location, and ‘formerly’ is not fully demonstrated; no semantic chronology is inferred from dictionary gloss order.
Baxter–Sagart and Unihan exact local rows were provided and checked, but official Unicode pages for both 在 and 才 were inaccessible. Local metadata does not substitute for an external Unihan citation.
The Sinica Xiaoxuetang query was reported unavailable with HTTP 401 in the supplied input; its license page returned no readable terms in this session.

No usable new historical glyph image was established. Existing 在 oracle and seal image candidates failed acquisition with HTTP 404 and cannot be reused in this run; the exact direct image alternatives could not be verified.

limitations.text: No verifiable glyph image is available to illustrate 在’s debated early forms: the identified oracle-script and seal-script images could not be retrieved, and no alternative exact image with verified reuse terms was established. The written accounts also disagree about whether early forms used 才 alone or 才 with 士, so the graphic sequence remains uncertain.
